headline: Data Centers Pay Own Grid Costs
short_summary: This bill shifts the financial responsibility for new grid infrastructure from residential ratepayers to large energy users, primarily data centers, ensuring they bear the costs associated with their significant energy demands.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP1123) on 2026-05-14
opponents: Data center industry, large energy users
news_headline: Gov. Spanberger signs legislation aimed at addressing high energy costs, rejoins RGGI
news_summary: Governor Abigail Spanberger signed a package of legislation to address high energy costs and ensure data centers do not drive up costs for families. This includes protecting Virginia ratepayers from shouldering the cost of new energy infrastructure investments by data centers and other high load energy customers.

headline: Data Center Water Use Reporting Mandate
short_summary: This bill requires data centers to report their water consumption, providing transparency and data for future water resource management and environmental policy decisions.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP0896) on 2026-04-13
supporters: Environmental groups, water conservation advocates, local governments
news_headline: New Virginia law requires data center water usage be made public
news_summary: A new Virginia law, championed by Senator Kannan Srinivasan, requires local water authorities to report data center water usage. This aims to provide transparency and make credible water consumption numbers accessible on the Department of Environmental Quality's website.

headline: Data Center Siting and Noise Regulations
short_summary: This bill establishes new regulations for the siting of data centers and imposes limits on noise pollution, aiming to mitigate community impacts and ensure more responsible development.
status: Last Action: Incorporated by Counties, Cities and Towns (HB153-Thomas) (Voice Vote) on 2026-01-23
supporters: Local communities, residents near proposed data center sites, environmental groups
opponents: Data center industry, real estate developers
news_headline: A Roanoke Delegate Helped Write Virginia's New Data Center Law. Here's What It Does, and What It Doesn't
news_summary: This new Virginia law, effective July 1, 2026, requires developers of large data centers to conduct site assessments examining noise impacts on nearby residential units and schools. While it mandates studies and utility disclosures, the law does not set specific noise limits, water caps, or setbacks.
